product: Pre-production developer: 50% of Ambler Metals LLC, which owns 100% of the Upper Kobuk Mineral Projects in northwestern Alaska, comprising the Arctic copper-zinc-lead-gold-silver VMS deposit (about 5% copper-equivalent per the January 2023 feasibility study) and the Bornite copper-cobalt deposit.
demand: No sales today. The thesis is forward demand: the US imports a substantial share of its copper, Wood Mackenzie projects global copper consumption up 24% by 2035 on electrification and AI data centres, and S&P Global sees data centres at up to 14% of US electricity demand by 2030.
pricing_power: None evidenced. TMQ is a future price-taking commodity producer with no offtake terms disclosed; Arctic's roughly 5% copper-equivalent grade would give a low-cost, high-margin position if built, but that is potential, not realised pricing power.
competition: Competing copper developers and operating US mines (Freeport-McMoRan, Rio Tinto, Ivanhoe Electric, Arizona Sonoran, NovaGold Donlin Gold) plus imported concentrate; also rival Alaska critical-minerals projects competing for the same FAST-41 permitting slots and federal capital.
team: President and CEO Tony Giardini; Ron Rimelman appointed President of Ambler Metals in June 2026, with 40 years of permitting experience, ex-VP EHS and Sustainability at NOVAGOLD on Donlin Gold, MIT chemical engineering; Richard Gosse, VP Exploration, is Qualified Person; Matthew Keevil is VP Investor Relations.
market_strategy: Leverage US critical-minerals policy, namely FAST-41 Covered Project status, a published federal-state permitting timetable, an about 10% US Department of War equity stake and a proposed 211-mile AIDEA road, to de-risk Arctic to a construction decision, then develop the wider 100-kilometre Ambler VMS belt with South32.
bull: US Department of War took ~10% equity via $35.6M closed Sep 11 2026; FAST-41 timetable published Jul 2026 targets draft EIS Oct 2027 and ROD Sep 2028; Arctic is ~5% Cu-equivalent with South32 as 50/50 JV partner.
bear: Zero revenue, H1 FY2026 net loss $13.4M, Q2 EPS -$0.04 missed consensus; Aug 5 2026 Freedom Capital and UBS both downgraded to Hold; $200M ATM and $0.01 warrants imply dilution; Ambler Road litigation pending.
falsifier: A company-dated disclosure before Oct 2027 showing the USACE NEPA schedule slipped past the Oct 2027 draft EIS target, or Ambler Road litigation halting access.
web_what_changed: Last 90 days: Jul 8 Q2 FY2026 results (net loss $6.3M; cash $38.8M at May 31); Jul 13-16 federal-state FAST-41 permitting schedule published (draft EIS Oct 2027, ROD Sep 2028); Aug 28 definitive Department of War investment agreements; Sep 11 closed US$35.6M DOW investment, US government about 10% holder; Sep 21 USACE Notice of Intent launching NEPA review.
web_not_known_yesterday: Not found. No company or regulatory event dated Sep 22-25 2026; the latest primary item remains the Sep 21 2026 USACE Notice of Intent. Sep 24 brought only aggregator consensus recaps (Moderate Buy) and an unconfirmed Sep 29 Q3 earnings estimate from MarketBeat, not a company-dated event.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: No growth to decompose: zero revenue, so neither price nor volume. Value rests on future copper demand (Wood Mackenzie sees global consumption plus 24% by 2035 on electrification and AI data centres; S&P Global sees data centres up to 14% of US power demand by 2030) and on permitting milestones, not realised mix.
web_suppliers: No supplier contracts disclosed. Inputs are two diamond drill rigs and drilling, geotechnical and environmental contractors for the 2026 program plus fuel and camp logistics; access would depend on the proposed 211-mile Ambler Road held by AIDEA. Remote road-less location and short seasonal access are the binding constraints.
web_customers: None today, no production or revenue. Future product would be Arctic copper-zinc-lead-gold-silver and Bornite copper-cobalt concentrates; no offtake agreements announced. South32 is the 50/50 joint venture partner, not a contracted customer. Customer concentration: not found.
web_who_loses: Foreign copper producers and concentrate exporters whose US market share a domestic Alaska mine would displace; rival US critical-minerals projects competing for the same FAST-41 permitting slots and federal equity (for example NovaGold Donlin Gold, Contango Ore Johnson Tract, Graphite One, Northern Dynasty Pebble). Also short sellers if the stock re-rates.
web_contradicting_evidence: Production is years away: ROD targeted Sep 2028, construction decision later, no revenue this decade. H1 FY2026 net loss $13.4M; Q2 EPS -$0.04 missed -$0.01 consensus. On Aug 5 2026 Freedom Capital cut to Hold, PT $6.20 to $4.30 on lower copper multiples, and UBS downgraded to Hold. South32's stake fell to 6.0%; a $200M ATM and $0.01 DOW warrants imply dilution; Ambler Road litigation pending.
web_if_management_right: The Notice of Intent leads to a draft EIS in Oct 2027, a Record of Decision in Sep 2028 and a construction decision, with federal help financing the 211-mile Ambler Road. Arctic, roughly 5% copper-equivalent, becomes a premier North American copper mine; Bornite adds 1.9 billion pounds of copper over 17 years, extending district mining past 30 years.
web_if_management_wrong: Permitting slips or Ambler Road litigation blocks access. Cash burn continues past $38.8M; the $200M ATM and $0.01 warrants dilute holders, the DOW derivative mark-to-market loss widens, and South32 may slow funding. First to break is liquidity and financing, then the credibility of the published permitting timetable, then the equity.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: AIDEA, which builds and owns the Ambler Road; NANA Regional Corporation and Doyon-region Alaska communities; Alaska construction, drilling, engineering and logistics contractors; Alaska state and Northwest Arctic Borough tax bases; South32 as 50% partner; and US smelters, refiners and defence or critical-minerals supply chains substituting domestic copper for imports.
